item.title: NASA’s Hubble Spies Spiral’s Edge
item.description: This NASA Hubble Space Telescope image features the edge-on, intermediate spiral galaxy NGC 1827, located roughly 37 million light-years away in the constellation Columba, the Dove.

item.title: NASA Satellites Observe Historic 2026 El Niño
item.description: A phenomenon rarer than a solar eclipse and more powerful than any single storm system is unfolding this fall, and NASA is tracking it closely. item.title: NASA Welcomes All Ages, Experience Levels for Space Apps Challenge
item.description: Registration is open for the 2026 NASA Space Apps Challenge, a two-day global event on Saturday, Nov. 14 and Sunday, Nov. 15, where teams work to create solutions inspired by NASA’s most ambitious exploration goals and making use of the agency’s free and open data. item.title: NASA Awards Enable Research, Technology to Build Future Workforce
item.description: NASA has selected 12 U.S. institutions to receive $12 million to accelerate academic research and technology development in support of the agency’s priorities for exploring the Moon, Mars, and deep space. item.title: Efficient numerical evolution of self-gravitating systems with dark-matter-baryon scattering
item.description: arXiv:2610.20702v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present a fast algorithm to numerically evolve a spherically symmetric system consisting of dark matter and gas, including dark-matter-baryon scattering. item.description: arXiv:2610.21951v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the stimulated capture of axion and axion-like particles around primordial black holes, mediated by quartic self-interactions. item.title: Compact Dark Matter with Globular Cluster Pulsars
item.description: arXiv:2610.20732v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Pulsars are exceptionally stable clocks, and a compact dark-matter object passing near the line of sight to a pulsar delays its pulses through the Shapiro effect. item.description: arXiv:2610.21041v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We consider the inelastic dark matter interpretation of the recent 248 keV event observed by LZ and identify different experiments that could test it. item.description: Video: 02:31:10 Watch the replay of the livestream originally broadcast on 3 September as ESA/JAXA's BepiColombo mission took the first critical step towards arriving at Mercury. item.title: Isaias Dims the Gulf Coast
item.description: High-definition images of nighttime lights show where the hurricane knocked out power along the Florida Panhandle and how quickly the lights came back.

item.title: NASA to Conduct Low-Altitude Flights Over Texas Farmland
item.description: A NASA Dynamic Aviation A200 aircraft will conduct low-flying research flights over farmland near Transit, Texas, from Thursday, Oct. 22, through Monday, Nov. 9. These flights will measure gaseous and particulate emissions from animal feeding operations. Agricultural emissions represent an important and understudied part of Earth’s land and atmosphere systems. The FarmFlux mission will deploy […]

item.title: Science begins for Smile
item.description: On 23 September, the European-Chinese Smile mission was declared ready to start revealing how Earth responds to the wind of charged particles from the Sun. This follows a busy in-space commissioning period since the spacecraft launched on 19 May and reached its target orbit for science operations on 20 June.

item.title: Roman lifts off on a mission to survey the infrared sky
item.description: Image: NASA’s Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope lifted off on a SpaceX Falcon Heavy rocket from NASA’s Kennedy Space Center in Florida, USA, at 07:26 EDT / 12:26 BST/ 13:26 CEST on 30 August 2026. With the successful launch, Roman began its mission to survey the sky in visible to near-infrared light to help reveal the nature of dark energy and dark matter. item.description: In January 2025, the LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA collaboration observed an exceptionally loud gravitational-wave signal: GW250114.
